summary: Preview of the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final between England and South Africa at the Stade de France on October 21, 2023. It covers kick-off times and broadcast options worldwide, both teams' paths to the last four, the confirmed lineups and the changes England made, and a prediction that the Springboks will win.
one_line: Preview of the England vs South Africa 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final with kick-off times, broadcasters, lineups and a Springboks win prediction.
key_facts: England and South Africa meet in the second semi-final of the 2023 Rugby World Cup at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, kicking off 9 p.m. local time on Saturday, October 21, 2023.
The kick-off is 3:00 p.m. ET in the USA and Canada, 8:00 p.m. BST in the UK, and 6:00 a.m. AEDT on Sunday, October 22 in Australia.

Broadcasters include Peacock in the USA, TSN in Canada, ITV in the UK, Channel 9 and Stan Sport in Australia, Sky GO in New Zealand, Fan Code in India and BeIN Sports in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore.
South Africa beat England 32-12 in the 2019 final, securing a record-equalling third title; it was the first final in which South Africa scored a try.
England are the only remaining side yet to lose at the tournament; they beat Argentina, Japan, Chile, Samoa and Fiji, the last by 30-24 in Marseille, with captain Owen Farrell kicking 20 points.
Only Japan and Chile were beaten with bonus points, and narrow wins over Samoa and Fiji showed England are 'gettable'.
South Africa lost 13-8 to Ireland in the pool stage, finishing second in Pool B, then beat hosts France 29-28 at the Stade de France in the quarter-final.

England make three changes: Freddie Steward returns at fullback, Manu Tuilagi starts at inside centre, Joe Marler replaces Ellis Genge at loosehead prop, and George Martin replaces Ollie Chessum in the second row.
South Africa are unchanged from the France game, with Eben Etzebth scoring the only second-half try; Kurt-Lee Arendse, Damian de Allende and Cheslin Kolbe scored first-half tries.
Kolbe's try came after Thomas Ramos had his conversion charged down, a two-point difference that proved crucial.
The last meeting was a 27-13 South Africa win at Twickenham, Eddie Jones's last game as England coach before Steve Borthwick was hired.
The article predicts South Africa will win, citing a huge step up in quality needed from Borthwick's England.
